issues.description: The problem specification and the solution expect a StockIngredient constructor with three parameters (String name, int price, int quantity). The template repository's StockIngredient class only provides a four-parameter constructor (String, int, int, boolean strictValidation). This prevents students from instantiating StockIngredient using the three-argument form required by the exercise and shown in the UML and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) to the template's StockIngredient class (or provide an overloaded constructor) that implements the expected validation/initialization. Alternatively, keep the existing four-argument constructor but add an overload that defaults the strictValidation parameter to match the behavior required by the problem and solution.

issues.description: Constructor signature for the StockIngredient entity differs across artifacts: the problem statement (UML) and the solution expect a 3-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), while the template repository provides a 4-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). This mismatch creates a conceptual and practical mapping problem for students (they are told about a 3-arg constructor but the provided template API differs), increasing extraneous cognitive load and risking compilation/usage confusion when implementing SealSaloon methods that instantiate StockIngredient.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor API consistent across artifacts. Either add a 3-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int) to the template (delegating to the existing strictValidation constructor or implementing the same validation as the solution), or update the problem statement/UML and the solution to document and use the 4-argument constructor. Preferably provide the 3-arg constructor in the template to match the UML and solution implementation.
